step1_analysis.description: A high-bandwidth differential pre-amplifier stage for a comparator. It features a differential input pair with diode-connected PMOS loads and parallel PMOS current sources to boost the DC gain without significantly degrading the bandwidth.

paper_reference.title: A 4-GHz Effective Sample Rate Integrated Test Core for Analog and Mixed-Signal Circuits

paper_reported.value: 65 dB (likely full system SNR/Gain, not single stage)

sky130_expected.calculation: gm_in = sqrt(2 * 270u * 10 * 52.5u) = 0.53 mS. gm_load = sqrt(2 * 50u * 10 * 32.9u) = 0.18 mS. Gain = gm_in / gm_load = 2.94 V/V = 9.3 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: A single-stage differential amplifier with diode-connected loads typically has low gain (around 10 dB). The 65 dB reported in the paper likely refers to the full comparator multi-stage gain or system SNR.

bandwidth_3db.description: Frequency at which the gain drops by 3 dB from its DC value

sky130_expected.calculation: R_out = 1 / gm_load = 5.5 kOhm. Assuming C_load = 10 fF, f_3dB = 1 / (2 * pi * R_out * C_load) = 2.89 GHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The diode-connected loads provide a low output impedance, pushing the dominant pole to the GHz range, which is necessary for a 4-GHz effective sample rate.

propagation_delay.description: Time delay between the input crossing zero and the output crossing zero

sky130_expected.calculation: Delay is roughly proportional to R_out * C_load. With R_out = 5.5 kOhm and C_load = 10 fF, tau = 55 ps. Actual delay includes slewing and intrinsic capacitances, typically 2-3x tau.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Matches the 200 ps reported in the paper, adjusted slightly for the faster 130nm process compared to the original 0.35um process.

power_consumption.description: Total static power dissipated by the circuit

paper_reported.value: 3 W or 7 W (likely mW in original paper)

sky130_expected.calculation: Tail current I_tail = 105 uA (with Vbias=0.7V). Total current from VDD is equal to I_tail. Power = 1.8V * 105uA = 189 uW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Calculated based on typical bias conditions for a high-speed pre-amplifier in 130nm. The '3 w' in the prompt is likely a parsing error for 3 mW for the entire test core.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC gain, 3dB bandwidth, propagation delay, and power consumption of the comparator pre-amplifier.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Pre-amplifier Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm3=5u L_xm3=0.5u
.param W_xm4=5u L_xm4=0.5u
.param W_xm5=5u L_xm5=0.5u
.param W_xm6=5u L_xm6=0.5u
.param W_xm7=5u L_xm7=0.5u

XM1 N0 N3 LABEL_NET_0 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 N2 N3 LABEL_NET_1 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM3 N2 N2 LABEL_NET_2 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}
XM4 N0 LABEL_NET_3 N1 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm4} w={W_xm4}
XM5 N1 LABEL_NET_4 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm5} w={W_xm5}
XM6 N2 LABEL_NET_5 N1 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm6} w={W_xm6}
XM7 N0 N0 LABEL_NET_6 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm7} w={W_xm7}

VVDD VDD 0 1.8
V_LABEL_NET_0 LABEL_NET_0 0 1.8
V_LABEL_NET_1 LABEL_NET_1 0 1.8
V_LABEL_NET_2 LABEL_NET_2 0 1.8
V_LABEL_NET_6 LABEL_NET_6 0 1.8

V_N3 N3 0 1.1
V_LABEL_NET_4 LABEL_NET_4 0 0.7

V_INP LABEL_NET_3 0 dc 0.9 ac 0.5 pulse(0.8 1.0 1n 50p 50p 2n 4n)
V_INN LABEL_NET_5 0 dc 0.9 ac -0.5 pulse(1.0 0.8 1n 50p 50p 2n 4n)

B1 OUT_DIFF 0 V=v(N2)-v(N0)
C1 N0 0 10f
C2 N2 0 10f

.control
  op
  let power = -i(VVDD)*1.8 - i(V_LABEL_NET_0)*1.8 - i(V_LABEL_NET_1)*1.8 - i(V_LABEL_NET_2)*1.8 - i(V_LABEL_NET_6)*1.8
  print power

  ac dec 100 1Meg 100Gig
  let gain_db = vdb(OUT_DIFF)
  meas ac dc_gain MAX gain_db
  meas ac f3db when gain_db='dc_gain - 3' fall=1

  tran 10p 5n
  meas tran t_delay trig v(LABEL_NET_3) val=0.9 rise=1 targ v(OUT_DIFF) val=0 rise=1
  
  quit
.endc
.end
